seoTitle: Gross Salary — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Gross salary is total earnings before deductions — basic pay plus allowances such as HRA, dearness allowance, special allowance and any bonus.
definition: Gross salary is total earnings before deductions — basic pay plus allowances such as HRA, dearness allowance, special allowance and any bonus. It sits between CTC and take-home pay.
bodyHtml:
Why Gross Salary matters

Gross salary is the base for most statutory calculations and the figure that appears at the top of a payslip. Employees usually quote it, employers usually quote CTC, and neither is take-home.

Gross Salary formula

Gross salary = Basic + HRA + DA + Allowances + Bonus

Net pay = gross salary − employee deductions − TDS.

How Gross Salary works in practice

Structure it deliberately, because the split between basic pay and allowances changes provident fund, gratuity and tax outcomes for both sides.

faq.question: Is gross salary the same as CTC?
faq.answer: No. CTC also includes employer contributions and provisions that never reach the employee.

faq.question: Does gross salary include overtime?
faq.answer: Overtime is usually shown separately as it varies month to month.
